Golda Meir. The fourth and first female prime minister of Israel, serving from nineteen sixty-nine to nineteen seventy-four. A labor socialist and early Zionist, Meir emigrated to Palestine from the Soviet Union by way of the United States in nineteen twenty-one and worked as a kibbutznik and labor organizer. She served as minister of labor and later foreign minister before becoming prime minister at age seventy-one. She led Israel during the Yom Kippur War in nineteen seventy-three, a sudden Egyptian-Syrian offensive that shocked the nation, though Israel recovered and won the conflict. Her popularity eroded after the war. She promoted Labour Party policies of government ownership, collective farms, and generous welfare, shaping Israel's social-democratic model. She oversaw the Munich Massacre at the nineteen seventy-two Olympic Games and authorized Operation Wrath of God, a covert retaliation campaign. After the Yom Kippur War inquiry, she resigned in nineteen seventy-four, her political downfall reflecting public disillusionment. Meir remained a cultural icon—modest, direct, and uncompromising—epitomizing Israeli pragmatism and toughness as a trailblazer in a male-dominated region, following in the footsteps of her predecessor and model, David Ben-Gurion.
